questions.question: The 'Palk Strait' lies between India and which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is a strait between the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and the Mannar district of Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal with the Gulf of Mannar. Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) lies across this strait.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Education?
questions.explanation: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002, provides for free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years as a Fundamental Right.

questions.question: Who founded the 'Asiatic Society of Bengal' in 1784?
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones, a British philologist and scholar, founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in Calcutta in January 1784 to promote Oriental research. He was the first to suggest that Sanskrit bore a resemblance to Greek and Latin.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate in India?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet (China), flows through Tibet as Yarlung Tsangpo, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, and then flows through Assam. Godavari, Krishna, and Narmada all originate within India.

questions.question: The Panchayati Raj system was constitutionalised through which Amendment to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 constitutionalised the Panchayati Raj system by adding Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) to the Constitution, providing for a three-tier system of local self-government at the village, intermediate, and district levels.

questions.question: The 'Jallikattu', a traditional bull-taming sport practised during the Pongal festival, is associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Jallikattu is an ancient Tamil sport associated with the Mattu Pongal festival in Tamil Nadu. It involves holding onto the hump of a bull for a set distance or time, or removing prizes tied to its horns.

questions.question: The 'Krishi Unnati Mela' and the 'Soil Health Card Scheme' are initiatives primarily related to which sector?
questions.explanation: The Soil Health Card Scheme (launched in 2015) provides farmers with a printed report of the nutrient status of their soil along with fertiliser recommendations. Krishi Unnati Mela is an agricultural fair to promote modern farming techniques. Both are agriculture-sector initiatives.

questions.question: Who was awarded the 'Bharat Ratna' in 2024, becoming the fifth person to receive it posthumously?
questions.explanation: Karpoori Thakur, former Chief Minister of Bihar and a champion of backward class reservation, was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in February 2024. He is the 50th recipient of India's highest civilian award.

questions.question: India and which country signed the 'Indus Waters Treaty' in 1960?
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed between India and Pakistan in September 1960, brokered by the World Bank. It allocates control over the Indus River and its tributaries between the two nations.

questions.question: India's third lunar mission, 'Chandrayaan-3', successfully landed near the south pole of the Moon in which year?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land near the south pole and the fourth country overall to achieve a soft landing on the Moon.

questions.question: The 'PM-JANMAN' scheme launched in 2023 is aimed at which section of society?
questions.explanation: PM-JANMAN (Prime Minister's Jan Jatiya Nyay Maha Abhiyan), launched on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas (November 2023), is aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

questions.question: Which Indian city hosted the 141st session of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 2023?
questions.explanation: The 141st IOC Session was held in Mumbai from 15 to 17 October 2023. During this session, the IOC approved the inclusion of cricket in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

questions.question: The 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup was jointly hosted by the USA and which other country?
questions.explanation: The 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup was jointly hosted by the USA and the West Indies.

questions.question: The 'Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar' scheme, a new science award framework replacing earlier awards, was introduced by the Government of India in which year?
questions.explanation: The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar scheme was notified in 2024, unifying various science awards into a single framework consisting of Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva, and Vigyan Team awards.

questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is: 1x2=2, 2x3=6, 3x4=12, 4x5=20, 5x6=30, so the next term is 6x7=42.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as 3120 and DOG is coded as 4157, then how would BAT be coded?
questions.explanation: Using alphabet positions: A=1, B=2, C=3,..., T=20. CAT = C(3)A(1)T(20) = 3120. BAT = B(2)A(1)T(20) = 2120.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards South, then turns right and walks 3 km. He then turns right again and walks 5 km. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Starting at O: Walks 5 km South to A. Turns right (faces West), walks 3 km to B. Turns right (faces North), walks 5 km to C. Point C is 3 km West of O. So he is West of the starting point.

questions.question: A man points to a woman and says, 'She is the sister of my father's only son.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: My father's only son is myself (assuming I have no brothers). The sister of myself is my sister. So the woman is the man's sister.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 121, 169, 196, 215
questions.explanation: 121 = 11^2, 169 = 13^2, 196 = 14^2 — all are perfect squares. 215 is not a perfect square (14^2 = 196, 15^2 = 225), so 215 is the odd one out.

questions.question: Book is to Read as Food is to:
questions.explanation: A book is meant to be read; similarly, food is meant to be eaten. The relationship is 'object : primary action on it'.

questions.question: At what time between 7:00 and 8:00 will the hands of a clock be in a straight line but not overlapping?
questions.explanation: For hands to be in a straight line (opposite direction), the minute hand must be 30 minute-spaces ahead of the hour hand. At 7:00, the hour hand is at 35 minute-spaces from 12. The minute hand gains 11/12 min-space per minute. Time = (35 - 30) / (11/12) = 5 x 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes past 7.

questions.question: In an election, a candidate who gets 65% of the total votes is elected by a majority of 1800 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.explanation: Winner: 65%, Loser: 35%. Majority = 65% - 35% = 30% of total = 1800. Total = 1800 / 0.30 = 6000 votes.

questions.question: What will be the simple interest on Rs.8000 at 5% per annum for 3 years?
questions.explanation: Simple Interest = P x R x T / 100 = 8000 x 5 x 3 / 100 = Rs.1200.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 27. If one number is excluded, the average becomes 25. What is the excluded number?
questions.explanation: Sum of 5 numbers = 27 x 5 = 135. Sum of 4 numbers = 25 x 4 = 100. Excluded number = 135 - 100 = 35.

questions.question: If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 8 : 9, then A : C equals:
A can complete a piece of work in 10 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. In how many days can they together complete the work?
questions.explanation: A's 1 day work = 1/10, B's 1 day work = 1/15. Together = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. So they complete the work in 6 days.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys 50 kg of rice for Rs.2000 and sells it at Rs.45 per kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Cost price per kg = Rs.2000/50 = Rs.40. Selling price per kg = Rs.45. Profit per kg = Rs.5. Profit % = (5/40) x 100 = 12.5%.

questions.question: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Speed = 72 km/h = 72 x (5/18) = 20 m/s. Time = 15 sec. Length of train = Speed x Time = 20 x 15 = 300 m.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on Rs.12000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
If 2x + 5 = 15, what is the value of x?
The perimeter of a square field is 80 m. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 x side = 80 m -> side = 20 m. Area = side^2 = 20^2 = 400 sq m.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 36 and 48?
What is the least number that when divided by 6, 9, 12, and 18 leaves a remainder of 2 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM(6, 9, 12, 18) = 36. Required number = LCM + remainder = 36 + 2 = 38.

questions.question: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 7 m and a height of 10 m. What is its capacity in cubic metres?
questions.explanation: Volume of cylinder = pi x r^2 x h = (22/7) x 7^2 x 10 = (22/7) x 49 x 10 = 22 x 7 x 10 = 1540 m3.

questions.question: A company's quarterly sales (in lakhs) are: Q1 = 25, Q2 = 35, Q3 = 30, Q4 = 40. What is the average quarterly sales?
A bag contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. If one ball is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is NOT red?
questions.explanation: Total balls = 10. P(NOT red) = P(blue) = 6/10 = 3/5.

questions.question: Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants. Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. All plants are roses. Which conclusion(s) logically follow(s)?
options: D) Both I and II follow
questions.explanation: From 'All roses are flowers' and 'All flowers are plants', we deduce 'All roses are plants' (I follows). But 'All plants is roses' cannot be concluded (II does not follow).

questions.question: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, and F are sitting in a circle facing the centre. A is between D and F, C is between E and B, and F is to the left of D. Who is sitting opposite A?
questions.explanation: Arranging in a circle: F-A-D (clockwise), C between E and B means B-C-E. So the order is F-A-D-B-C-E (clockwise). A is opposite E.

questions.question: If 1st January 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1st January 2025?
questions.explanation: 2024 is a leap year (366 days). 366 = 52 weeks + 2 days. So 1st January 2025 is 2 days after Monday = Wednesday.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'COMPUTER' is written as 'DPNQVUFS'. How would 'SCIENCE' be written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted by +1: C->D, O->P, M->N, P->Q, U->V, T->U, E->F, R->S. So SCIENCE -> TDJFOEF (S->T, C->D, I->J, E->F, N->O, C->D, E->F).

questions.question: All the students in a class are above 18 years. Ramesh is in that class. Which conclusion is valid?
options: A) Ramesh is the oldest in the class
questions.explanation: If all students are above 18 and Ramesh is in the class, it logically follows that Ramesh is above 18 years.

questions.question: Statement: 'Unless you study regularly, you cannot pass the examination.' Conclusions: I. Studying regularly ensures passing. II. Those who do not study regularly will not pass.
options: A) Both I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'Unless you study regularly, you cannot pass' means 'If you do not study regularly, you cannot pass' (II follows). It does NOT mean that studying regularly is the ONLY way to pass -- there could be other ways (I does not follow).

questions.question: In a class of 40 students, 25 play cricket and 20 play football. If 10 students play both games, how many play only football?
questions.explanation: Students playing only football = Total football players - Both = 20 - 10 = 10.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric charge is the Coulomb (C). Ampere is the unit of electric current, Volt is the unit of potential difference, and Ohm is the unit of resistance.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of methane?
questions.explanation: Methane is the simplest hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH4. CO2 is carbon dioxide, C2H6 is ethane, and C3H8 is propane.

questions.question: Which part of the plant is responsible for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis primarily occurs in the leaves, specifically in the chloroplast-containing cells (mesophyll cells) of the leaf. Chlorophyll in chloroplasts captures sunlight.

questions.question: The Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and biodiversity hotspot. Which of the following major peninsular rivers originates at Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Godavari River, the longest river of peninsular India, originates at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra within the Western Ghats range. The Narmada and Mahanadi originate in central India, and the Tapi originates in the Satpura range.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is known as 'marsh gas' and is produced by the decomposition of organic matter in marshy areas?
questions.explanation: Methane (CH4) is known as marsh gas. It is produced by the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in swamps, marshes, and coal mines (where it is called firedamp). Methane is also a major component of biogas.

questions.question: A body is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 49 m/s. How long will it take to reach the maximum height? (Take g = 9.8 m/s2)
questions.explanation: At maximum height, final velocity v = 0. Using v = u - gt, we get 0 = 49 - 9.8t. So t = 49/9.8 = 5 seconds.

questions.question: The 'Eutrophication' of water bodies leads to excessive growth of algae. Which of the following pollutants is primarily responsible for this phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is caused by the excessive enrichment of water bodies with nutrients, primarily nitrogen and phosphorus from agricultural runoff, sewage, and industrial effluents. This leads to algal blooms, oxygen depletion, and death of aquatic organisms.
